evals.name: drift-kinds
evals.hypothesis: H2, H8: checking sends a drift the specs or Bounds settle back to /write, and holds a choice the work list left open for the user.
evals.prompt:
/coding:inspect Check the round /coding:write just finished in the last commit. Earlier in this conversation I confirmed this work list:

| Order | # | The work |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | G1 | take the member discount off the order total |
| 2 | G2 | page the order list |
| 3 | G3 | export orders as CSV |

Bounds: page the order list by page number (`?page=2`), 20 orders a page.
References: docs/spec.md
evals.expected_output: Three drifts: the discount applied after tax (spec settles it, back to /write), cursor paging (Bounds settle it, back to /write), cancelled orders left out of the CSV (open choice, held for the user). Report opens with a neutral conclusion table.
evals.prediction: Baseline passes 1, 3, 5 and 10; it treats every drift alike, so 2, 4 and 6 are unstable, and it has no conclusion table (7, 8).
expectations: The report states that the member discount is taken off after tax, against docs/spec.md.
The report hands the discount-and-tax fix to /write instead of asking the user to decide it.
The report states that the order list pages by a cursor (`after_id`) instead of the page number the Bounds set.
The report hands the paging fix to /write instead of asking the user to decide it.
The report states that the CSV export leaves out cancelled orders, a choice the work list did not settle.
The report holds the cancelled-orders choice for the user, without judging it right or wrong and without telling /write to change it.
The report opens with a conclusion table before the findings table.
The conclusion states facts only and does not say whether the round may end or is unfinished.
Each finding id is introduced with a phrase saying what it is.
The run changes no file in the repository.

evals.name: naming
evals.hypothesis: H3, H9: the names lens catches names whose word class hides their role, and keeps names a convention fixes.
evals.prompt: /coding:inspect The last commit adds the project class. Check it before I build the translation workflow on top of it.
evals.expected_output: Flags `Held` (bare participle as a type), `translated` (an action named as a participle), `running` (a question that does not read as one), and `get_title` (`get_` on a query); keeps `inherited` and `to_s`.
evals.prediction: Regression check: iteration 1 showed the baseline catches these textbook names too; only reading naming.md differs.
expectations: The report flags `translated` as a name that hides an action that writes a file.
The report flags the class name `Held` as a bare participle that does not say what the type is.
The report flags `running` as a yes-or-no question that does not read as one in Ruby, such as `running?`.
The report flags `get_title` for its `get_` prefix on a query.
The report does not list `inherited` as a naming problem.
The report does not list `to_s` as a naming problem.
The run reads the skill's references/naming.md.

evals.name: contexts
evals.hypothesis: H4: with contexts visible only from directories and vocabulary, the lenses apply inside each one and only the interfaces between them are checked.
evals.prompt: /coding:inspect Next I want to add order tracking to Shipping. Prepare for it.
evals.expected_output: Flags `Shipment.from_order` reaching into `Sales::Order` internals; treats `Customer` and `Recipient` as separate by design despite their overlapping fields.
evals.prediction: With no recorded rule and overlapping fields, the baseline proposes merging Customer and Recipient in some runs (3, 4) and may miss the event as the boundary (2).
expectations: The report flags `Shipment.from_order` reading `@customer` out of `Sales::Order` with `instance_variable_get`.
The report ties that finding to the boundary between the contexts, such as building the shipment from the `OrderPlaced` event instead.
The report does not propose merging `Sales::Customer` and `Shipping::Recipient` or call them duplicated.
The report does not call the different names `Customer` and `Recipient` an inconsistency.

evals.name: settle-first
evals.hypothesis: Planning settles what the code or a run can settle before reporting, asks only what the user alone decides, and keeps measuring and waiting out of the work list.
evals.prompt: /coding:inspect The monthly report is slow. I suspect `Formatter.new` on every row is the cost and we may need to cache formatters, but I'm not sure it's worth it. Prepare this round.
evals.expected_output: Runs the benchmark, finds the per-row `categories.find` lookup is the cost (formatter is ~2 ms of ~0.6 s), notes `FormatterCache` already exists, and gives a work list of changes with no measuring step, no waiting on the user, and no question the repo settles.
evals.prediction: The old skill says it does not run code, so it leaves the cost unrun and turns it into a measuring item or a question (1, 2, 4); 3 and 6 may pass for both.
expectations: The response reports timings it obtained by running the benchmark or a Ruby timing command in this run.
The response identifies the per-row `@categories.find` lookup as the main cost, rather than `Formatter.new`.
The response notes that `FormatterCache` already exists in lib/formatter_cache.rb.
No work list item consists only of measuring, benchmarking, profiling, or confirming something.
No work list item waits on the user (to notify, approve, choose, or run something) or on a measurement result still to come.
Still unknown contains no question that the repository or a run of its benchmark could answer, such as whether formatter creation is the cost or whether to measure first.
The run changes no file in the repository.
